purpose: Durable session-start, visual-authority, continuity, and sequential-production contract for Division Threshold image production.

authority.storyUnit: The exact assembled RexPrompt recipe controls what happens on the current page.
authority.releasedVisualCanon: StarSplitterVisions main must be checked at session start. Division Threshold currently has no released issue or released visual canon; do not invent one from prior chat generations.
authority.currentProduction: Only clearly approved current-production artwork stored against its exact recipe key may establish post-start visual state. Failed, rejected, repeated, superseded, intake-only, promotional, or merely generated images are not continuity authority.
authority.immediateContinuity: The immediately preceding approved page may establish carried state, but after a visual baseline exists it is never the sole identity, world, or style reference.

textualProductionBaseline.rule: Until approved artwork exists, these assembler-visible identity and world constraints define a clean visual start but are not a substitute for actual approved visual references once those references exist.

characterIdentity.cleanStart: Use assembler-visible visualAnchor, performance, and continuity-lock fields for the six locked leads. Do not infer alternate designs from genre convention or remembered chat images.
characterIdentity.afterApproval: Select the clearest approved durable appearance of every recurring character required by the current recipe and use text anchors to protect details that are unclear visually.
characterIdentity.rule: A newly generated appearance does not become identity authority merely because it is the newest image. It must pass production review and be explicitly approved/stored.

worldAndLocation.primary: Use the assembled page setting/settingText, region/regionText, and faction context together with the corresponding persistent shelves.
worldAndLocation.rule: Recurring locations retain one visual identity across camera changes. Split-location and montage pages must preserve the distinct established spaces named by the assembled recipe rather than averaging them into one generic Stack environment.

storyPageLanguage.cleanStart: Use the Division Threshold generation line and assembled page requirements for the first approved page. Establish a prestige portrait sequential-art language grounded in the Stack's accumulated infrastructure, readable physical geography, restrained institutional design, and non-superhero posthuman bodies.
storyPageLanguage.afterApproval: Use a selective set of the strongest approved ordinary story pages to stabilize rendering density, palette, gutters, lettering, architecture and panel language.
exclude: promotional lineups or labeled cast graphics
production annotations, contact sheets or comparison montages
failed, rejected, repeated or superseded generations

currentProduction.rule: An image is not durable production authority until it is explicitly approved and stored against its exact recipe key.

untrustedProductionSources: contact sheets or labeled character graphics not explicitly approved as scoped references
remembered visual descriptions when durable production data is available
sessionStartGate: Resolve the requested Division Threshold issue and ordered RexPrompt recipes from the current repository.
Check StarSplitterVisions main for a released Division Threshold baseline; if none exists, remain in clean visual-start mode rather than substituting chat history.
Resolve approved durable Division Threshold references and recipe-level drafts from production/references and production/drafts/manifest.json.
If no approved visual baseline exists, build the first page only from the exact assembled recipe plus current character, setting, region and faction production data.
After approved visual references exist, build a small working Visual Reference Set from the strongest relevant approved pages/references plus immediate continuity.
For every recurring character or recurring location required by the next page, use an actual approved visual reference whenever one exists.
Derive the production frontier; never resume from a remembered cursor or from the last image visible in chat.
perPageGate: Retrieve or assemble the exact current RexPrompt page recipe.
Verify that the selected page has not already been successfully produced, approved, or released.
Identify every recurring character, location, costume, prop and carried story state required by the recipe.
Select approved visual references for recurring elements whenever such references exist; otherwise use the normalized assembler-visible baseline without inventing competing canon.
Inspect the immediately preceding approved page when spatial, physical, emotional, environmental or object state carries forward.
Generate only after recipe, reference authority and immediate continuity are resolved.
Run reader, recipe-fidelity, character-continuity, spatial/prop, visual-language, composition and lettering checks.
Repair the smallest failing unit and do not advance while the page is defective.
After explicit approval, store the page as the approved production draft for its exact recipe key before relying on it as durable current-production state.

order: clearly successful/approved unpublished production with durable approval evidence
latest released StarSplitterVisions production when it exists
frontierPolicy.rule: The first scripted page not successfully produced is the production frontier. Failed, rejected, repeated, superseded or unusable generations do not advance it.
frontierPolicy.currentDurableState: Division Threshold is unreleased and production/drafts/manifest.json currently contains no approved Division Threshold recipe-level drafts. Absent stronger explicit approval evidence, the clean production frontier is DT_E001_P01.

storyPageOutputRule: A normal scripted Division Threshold unit is a finished full-color portrait prestige science-fiction comic page. Do not add a series title, issue header, page label, character name/handle label, dossier frame, credits, promotional callout, infographic heading or other non-scripted text. Only text required by the assembled recipe belongs on the story page.
